Before I make my final decision on process-water allocation, I need to hear updates from quality, maintenance, and EHS. Who'd like to start?

transcript.text: I'd like to start with the quality update. My lab test, completed this morning but not yet uploaded to the shared quality folder, found reclaimed-water conductivity at 1,800 microsiemens per centimeter. Line X's process limit is 1,200, while Line Y's process limit is 2,200. Line Y's scheduled batch requires exactly 1,800 liters, so reclaimed water is acceptable for that batch only after a conductivity test is recorded.

transcript.text: Here's the maintenance update. My inspection of the recovery skid — documented in my maintenance notebook but not yet entered in the work-order system — found that the skid requires an exact 3-hour membrane flush before use, and after that flush it can deliver reclaimed water at no more than 600 liters per hour. That's important for planning: if we need to use the recovery skid during the restriction, we need to account for both the 3-hour flush downtime and the 600 liters/hour delivery rate limit.

decisions.reclaimed_water_plan: Allocate 1,800 liters of reclaimed water to Line Y for its scheduled batch, as conductivity (1,800 µS/cm) is within Line Y's process limit of 2,200 µS/cm. Do not allocate reclaimed water to Line X, as conductivity exceeds Line X's 1,200 µS/cm limit. Before delivery, complete the 3-hour membrane flush on the recovery skid, adjust residual sanitizer to exactly 0.3 ppm, and obtain a signed sanitizer log for each use day. Ravi must upload the conductivity test result to the shared quality folder to formally record it before reclaimed water is used.

commitments.detail: Upload the completed conductivity test result (1,800 µS/cm) to the shared quality folder before any reclaimed water is delivered to Line Y.
Enter the recovery skid inspection findings into the work-order system, including the 3-hour flush requirement and 600 liters/hour delivery rate limit.
Attach the municipal permit review findings to the site's permit record and prepare a signed sanitizer log for each day reclaimed water is used during the 48-hour restriction.
Schedule and complete the 3-hour membrane flush on the recovery skid before reclaimed water delivery begins. At 600 liters/hour, delivering 1,800 liters will take 3 hours after the flush.
Adjust residual sanitizer in the reclaimed water to exactly 0.3 ppm before delivery to Line Y.
